# Get-ZbxItemPrototype

## SYNOPSIS

Gets the item prototypes that discovery rules turn into items.

## SYNTAX

## DESCRIPTION

An item prototype is the pattern a discovery rule turns into one item per entity it finds, such as the used space of each file system. The Get-ZbxItemPrototype cmdlet reads them with itemprototype.get: all of them up to -Limit, by name with -Name (* and ? are wildcards), by id with -Id or from the pipeline, or with the whole itemprototype.get selection in -Filter. -Template, -Host, -Discovery and the other object filters narrow the result to the item prototypes of the objects given, each a name, an id or a piped object. It writes ZabbixItemPrototype objects, with their related objects when a -Select switch asks for them, or, with -CountOutput, the number of matches; it needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Get an item prototype by name

```powershell
Get-ZbxItemPrototype -Name 'Used space on {#FSNAME}'
```

Gets the item prototype named Used space on {#FSNAME}. A * or ? in -Name makes it a search, so -Name 'Used*' gets every item prototype whose name starts with Used.

### Example 2: Get the item prototypes of a host

```powershell
Get-ZbxItemPrototype -Host 'web-01'
```

Gets the item prototypes of the host web-01. -Host takes a name, an id or an object; a host piped from Get-ZbxHost binds to it by its HostId property.

### Example 3: Search item prototypes with a filter

```powershell
Get-ZbxItemPrototype -Filter @{ search = @{ name = 'Used' }; limit = 10 }
```

-Filter takes the whole itemprototype.get selection, keyed by the API's field names: here at most ten item prototypes whose name contains Used.
